questions.q: What does a Streams + Tasks incremental pipeline MERGE from, compared to a typical full-table sync?
options: A stream containing only the rows that actually changed, not the entire source table
A random sample of the source table each run
A completely different database each time
Only rows that have never changed
questions.explain: The MERGE reads from a stream, which contains only what changed since it was last consumed — not the full source table.

questions.q: What does gating a task with `WHEN SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA(...)` achieve in this kind of pipeline?
options: The task's warehouse doesn't spin up and no work happens when there's nothing new in the stream
It forces the task to run twice as often
It deletes the stream after each check
It disables the MERGE statement permanently
questions.explain: SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA lets the task skip its run entirely, avoiding unnecessary warehouse spin-up, when there's no new data to process.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect a stream's metadata columns to SCD Type 2 (from Lesson 29)?
options: METADATA$ACTION and METADATA$ISUPDATE tell you exactly which rows changed and how, which is what SCD Type 2 needs to close out an old row version and insert a new one
Streams have no relationship to SCD logic at all
SCD Type 2 requires disabling streams entirely
METADATA$ACTION replaces the need for a MERGE statement
questions.explain: A stream's action/update flags map directly onto the 'what changed and how' information SCD Type 2 logic needs to run continuously.

questions.q: How can you verify, in Snowsight, that a Streams+Tasks pipeline is actually processing incrementally rather than reprocessing everything?
options: Filter Query History to 'Queries executed by user tasks' and check that each MERGE's rows-affected count tracks the size of actual changes, not the whole source table
There is no way to verify this in Snowflake
Check the warehouse's credit balance only
Only by reading the task's DDL definition, never its run results
questions.explain: Filtering Query History to task-executed queries lets you inspect each run's actual MERGE and its rows-affected count to confirm incremental behavior.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what MERGE pattern does the Streams+Tasks pipeline's SQL reuse from earlier in the course?
options: The same MERGE pattern from Lesson 9, now fed by a stream instead of a full source table
A completely new syntax unrelated to any earlier lesson
The COPY INTO pattern from Chapter 3
The window function pattern from Lesson 7
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly notes this is the same MERGE pattern from Lesson 9 — the difference is that it now merges from a stream of changes rather than a full table.
